title: Recursive / Fixed-Point Interaction

basis.scope: Define bounded interaction between recursive continuation semantics and fixed-point semantics without asserting universal convergence or universal reachability.

core_rule.statement: RecFix(C) is classified as AlignRecFix(C) only when Rec(C), EvalPhi(C), and Fix(C) are declared in compatible continuation domains and bounded under the same evaluation regime; bounded recursive/fixed-point interaction remains diagnostic, and RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Define the bounded interaction between recursive continuation semantics and fixed-point semantics without asserting that recursion always converges to a fixed point.

canonical_claims.statement: Recursive/fixed-point interaction is bounded and applies only inside the declared comparison regime.
AlignRecFix(C) requires equivalent continuation semantics under bounded recursive unfolding and fixed-point evaluation.
DivRecFix(C) records bounded mismatch without implying universal failure or global divergence.
FailRecFix(C) classifies interaction failure when typing, boundedness, or comparison cannot be satisfied.

adds: Bounded comparison of recursive and fixed-point semantics
does_not_add: Universal recursive reachability of fixed points

formal_objects.name: Recursive Fixed-Point Interaction
formal_objects.definition: The bounded semantic relation between recursive continuation evaluation Rec(C) and fixed-point evaluation EvalPhi(C).

formal_objects.name: Recursive Fixed-Point Alignment
formal_objects.definition: The condition where recursive continuation unfolding and fixed-point evaluation preserve the same continuation semantics within the declared bounded regime.

formal_objects.name: Recursive Fixed-Point Divergence
formal_objects.definition: The classified condition where recursive unfolding does not align with bounded fixed-point evaluation.

formal_objects.name: Recursive Fixed-Point Interaction Failure
formal_objects.definition: The failure state produced when recursive/fixed-point interaction cannot be typed, bounded, or evaluated under the declared regime.

interaction_rule.statement: RecFix(C) is admitted only when Rec(C), EvalPhi(C), and Fix(C) are declared in compatible continuation domains, bounded under the same evaluation regime, and their evaluated continuation semantics can be compared without altering RT_core.

alignment_rule.statement: AlignRecFix(C) holds when bounded recursive unfolding Rec(C) and bounded fixed-point evaluation EvalPhi(C) preserve equivalent continuation semantics for C.

divergence_rule.statement: DivRecFix(C) holds when Rec(C) is well-formed and bounded, but its recursive unfolding does not preserve equivalent continuation semantics with EvalPhi(C).

failure_conditions: C is not typed in a compatible continuation domain.
Recursive unfolding exceeds its declared bound.
Fixed-point evaluation exceeds its declared bound.
Rec(C) and EvalPhi(C) cannot be compared under a shared evaluation regime.
non_claims: Does not assert that recursion always reaches a fixed point.
Does not assert that every fixed point is recursively reachable.
Does not assert universal recursive convergence.
governance_notes: This patch is an interaction layer only.
It connects Rec(C) and Fix(C) without collapsing them into the same object.
Alignment, divergence, and failure are distinct outcomes.
Recursive unfolding remains separate from fixed-point correctness and uniqueness.
